name: MAX31856 universal thermocouple amplifier
description: Analog Devices (Maxim) MAX31856 thermocouple-to-digital converter for B, E, J, K, N, R, S and T thermocouples: cold-junction compensation and linearization on chip, 19-bit thermocouple temperature (0.0078125 C/LSB), 14-bit cold-junction temperature (0.015625 C/LSB), 50/60 Hz filtering and fault detection over SPI (CPHA = 1). Chip runs on 3.0-3.6 V; the breakout has a regulator and level shifting for 3-5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Universal Thermocouple Amplifier MAX31856 Breakout (product 3263), 9-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCK, SDO, SDI, CS, FLT, DRDY, 2-pin screw terminal for the thermocouple (+/-).
eli5: Reads almost any kind of thermocouple probe, from freezer cold to kiln hot, and reports the temperature in degrees.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3-5 V into the on-board 3.3 V regulator; use the same voltage as your logic (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCK
pins.description: SPI clock into the MAX31856 (up to 5 MHz, CPHA = 1: SPI mode 1 or 3)

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: SPI data out of the MAX31856 (to the board's MISO)

pins.name: SDI
pins.description: SPI data into the MAX31856 (from the board's MOSI); needed to set the thermocouple type and start conversions

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Chip select, active low; a 1-shot conversion starts when CS goes high after setting 1SHOT

pins.name: FLT
pins.description: FAULT output, active low (open thermocouple, over/undervoltage, threshold faults); optional

pins.name: DRDY
pins.description: Data-ready output, active low when a new conversion result is available; optional (the driver waits the conversion time instead)

supplierQuery: MAX31856 universal thermocouple amplifier breakout SPI
buildNotes: SPI with CPHA = 1 (mode 1 or 3), MSB first, up to 5 MHz; registers are read at 0Xh and written at 8Xh, and the address auto-increments in a multibyte transfer.
Set the thermocouple type in CR1 (01h) bits 3:0: B=0, E=1, J=2, K=3 (default), N=4, R=5, S=6, T=7; bits 6:4 select 1-16 averaged samples.
1-shot reading: write CR0 (80h) with 1SHOT (bit 6) set; the conversion starts when CS goes high and takes up to 155 ms (60 Hz filter) or 185 ms (50 Hz) plus open-circuit test time.
Thermocouple temperature: 19-bit two's complement in 0Ch-0Eh (bits 23..5), 0.0078125 C/LSB; read all three bytes in one transfer.
Cold-junction temperature: 14-bit two's complement in 0Ah-0Bh (bits 15..2), 0.015625 C/LSB.
Fault Status (0Fh): bit 0 open thermocouple, bit 1 input over/undervoltage, bits 2-7 range and threshold faults.
Leave 3Vo unconnected: it is the regulator's output, not an input. The thermocouple goes in the screw terminal; with K-type (US colours) yellow to +, red to -.

driver.code:
# MAX31856 precision thermocouple-to-digital converter (Analog Devices / Maxim), MicroPython driver.
# Written from datasheet 19-7534: SPI with CPHA = 1 (mode 1 or 3), registers read at 0Xh and written at 8Xh,
# address auto-increments during a multibyte transfer. Normally-off mode with 1-shot conversions.
# Thermocouple temperature: 19-bit signed in 0Ch..0Eh (bits 23..5), 0.0078125 C/LSB.
# Cold-junction temperature: 14-bit signed in 0Ah..0Bh (bits 15..2), 0.015625 C/LSB.
from machine import Pin
import time

_CR0 = 0x00
_CR1 = 0x01
_MASK = 0x02
_CJTH = 0x0A
_LTCBH = 0x0C
_SR = 0x0F

# CR0 bits
_ONE_SHOT = 0x40
_OCFAULT_01 = 0x10  # open-circuit detection, RS < 5 kohm
_FILTER_50HZ = 0x01

TYPES = {'B': 0, 'E': 1, 'J': 2, 'K': 3, 'N': 4, 'R': 5, 'S': 6, 'T': 7}
_AVG = {1: 0, 2: 1, 4: 2, 8: 3, 16: 4}

_FAULTS = ((0x80, 'cold junction out of range'), (0x40, 'thermocouple out of range'),
           (0x20, 'cold junction high'), (0x10, 'cold junction low'),
           (0x08, 'thermocouple high'), (0x04, 'thermocouple low'),
           (0x02, 'input over/undervoltage'), (0x01, 'thermocouple open'))


class MAX31856:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs, tc_type='K', filter_hz=60, samples=1):
        """spi: machine.SPI with phase=1 (mode 1 or 3), up to 5 MHz. cs: GPIO number of CS.
        tc_type: 'B', 'E', 'J', 'K', 'N', 'R', 'S' or 'T'. filter_hz: 50 or 60 (mains notch).
        samples: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 thermocouple samples averaged per conversion."""
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self._cr0 = _OCFAULT_01 | (_FILTER_50HZ if filter_hz == 50 else 0)  # normally-off, CJ sensor on
        self._write(_CR0, self._cr0)
        self._write(_CR1, (_AVG[samples] << 4) | TYPES[tc_type.upper()])
        self._write(_MASK, 0x00)  # let every fault assert the FLT pin
        # tCONV max 155 ms (60 Hz) / 185 ms (50 Hz), + open-circuit test (15 ms max),
        # + (samples - 1) x 33.33 ms (60 Hz) or 40 ms (50 Hz) when averaging
        per = 40 if filter_hz == 50 else 34
        self._conv_ms = (185 if filter_hz == 50 else 155) + 15 + (samples - 1) * per + 10

    def _write(self, reg, val):
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([0x80 | reg, val & 0xFF]))
        self.cs.value(1)

    def _read(self, reg, n):
        buf = bytearray(n + 1)
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write_readinto(bytes([reg & 0x7F]) + bytes(n), buf)
        self.cs.value(1)
        return buf[1:]

    def fault(self):
        """Fault Status register (0Fh); 0 = no fault."""
        return self._read(_SR, 1)[0]

    def convert(self):
        """Start a 1-shot conversion (it begins when CS goes high) and wait for it to finish."""
        self._write(_CR0, self._cr0 | _ONE_SHOT)
        time.sleep_ms(self._conv_ms)

    def thermocouple(self):
        """Linearized, cold-junction-compensated thermocouple temperature in C from the last conversion.
        Raises OSError on an open thermocouple or an input over/undervoltage."""
        d = self._read(_LTCBH, 4)  # 0Ch, 0Dh, 0Eh, then 0Fh (fault status) in one transfer
        sr = d[3]
        if sr & 0x03:
            raise OSError('MAX31856 fault: ' + ', '.join(n for b, n in _FAULTS if sr & b))
        raw = ((d[0] << 16) | (d[1] << 8) | d[2]) >> 5
        if raw & 0x40000:
            raw -= 0x80000
        return raw * 0.0078125

    def cold_junction(self):
        """Cold-junction (chip) temperature in C."""
        d = self._read(_CJTH, 2)
        raw = ((d[0] << 8) | d[1]) >> 2
        if raw & 0x2000:
            raw -= 0x4000
        return raw * 0.015625

    def read(self):
        """Run one conversion and return (thermocouple C, cold junction C)."""
        self.convert()
        return self.thermocouple(), self.cold_junction()

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SoftSPI
import time
from max31856 import MAX31856

# SoftSPI works on any pins of an ESP32 or Pico; the MAX31856 needs CPHA = 1 (phase=1)
spi = SoftSPI(baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=1, sck=Pin({SCK}), mosi=Pin({SDI}), miso=Pin({SDO}))
tc = MAX31856(spi, {CS}, tc_type='K', filter_hz=60)
while True:
    t, cj = tc.read()
    print('TC=%.2fC CJ=%.2fC' % (t, cj))
    time.sleep(1)
